name: Free Fibula Osteocutaneous Flap

classification.cormack_lamberty: Type D (osteomyofasciocutaneous extension via posterior crural septum)

dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired venae comitantes of peroneal artery

pedicle_length_cm.note: Lengthened up to 12 cm by discarding proximal bone

perforators.label: Distal Posterior Crural Septal Perforator
perforators.location: Junction of middle and distal thirds of fibula along posterior border
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Courses in posterior crural septum between soleus and peroneus longus

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Dual endosteal (nutrient artery) and segmental periosteal blood supply enables multiple closing-wedge osteotomies.
vascular_variants: Peronea arteria magna (~1–5%): single-vessel foot supply — ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION; preoperative CTA/MRA mandatory

motor: Common peroneal nerve wraps around fibular neck — leave ≥6–8 cm proximal fibula
sensory: Sural nerve posteriorly; superficial peroneal nerve anteriorly
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Mild lateral leg hypoesthesia; avoid peroneal nerve palsy.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Up to 22–25 cm dense bicortical bone suitable for dental implants; preserve ≥6–8 cm proximal and distal fibula.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Transferred as a free osteocutaneous flap to mandible, maxilla, or long-bone defects.

indications: Gold standard for segmental mandibular reconstruction (>6 cm or anterior symphysis)
Long-bone intercalary defects (tumor resection, osteomyelitis, pseudarthrosis)
contraindications: Peronea arteria magna or severe two-vessel tibial occlusive disease on CTA/MRA
Deep venous insufficiency or severe prior lower leg trauma
advantages: Longest available vascularized cortical bone (22–25 cm) supporting osseointegrated dental implants
Segmental periosteal blood supply permits multiple osteotomies
disadvantages: Risk of ankle instability if <6–8 cm distal fibula remains; STSG often required if paddle >4–5 cm

donor_site.closure: Primary closure if ≤4–5 cm (never under tension — compartment syndrome risk); otherwise STSG.
morbidity: Ankle valgus if distal remnant too short
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal adult gait disturbance when 6–8 cm proximal and distal bone preserved.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with hip/knee flexed and bump under ipsilateral buttock under tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Handheld Doppler along posterior fibular border
technique.design: Draw fibular head–lateral malleolus line; mark 6–8 cm proximal/distal safety zones; center paddle over junction of middle and distal thirds.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise anterior margin subfascially to expose posterior crural septum and septocutaneous perforators.
2. Detach peroneus muscles leaving 1–2 mm periosteal cuff and enter anterior compartment.
3. Perform proximal and distal osteotomies leaving ≥6–8 cm at both ends.
4. Divide interosseous membrane and ligate distal peroneal vessels.
5. Dissect tibialis posterior and FHL off posterior bone while protecting medial peroneal pedicle.
6. Complete VSP osteotomies on perfused leg, then divide proximal peroneal pedicle.
pearls: Discard proximal excess bone subperiosteally to lengthen pedicle by 4–6 cm.
Never close lateral leg skin tightly — skin-graft generously to prevent compartment syndrome.
pitfalls: Failing to rule out peronea arteria magna on preoperative CTA/MRA.

name: Profunda Artery Perforator (PAP) Flap

dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired venae comitantes of profunda perforator

perforators.label: Dominant Posterior Thigh Perforator
perforators.location: 3–6 cm inferior to gluteal crease, posterior to gracilis
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Emerges through adductor magnus medial to hamstrings

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Good-caliber paired venae comitantes; avoids medial groin lymphatics.
vascular_variants: Variable dominant perforator location — MRA/CTA strongly recommended

sensory: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (preserve to avoid sitting dysesthesia)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Provides ~250–450 g soft fat per side; can be stacked bilaterally.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Primary secondary autologous breast reconstruction flap when abdomen is unavailable.

indications: Autologous breast reconstruction when abdominal donor site is unavailable
Stacked bilateral PAP flaps for unilateral breast volume
advantages: Preserves gracilis muscle and spares inguinal lymphatics (minimal lymphedema risk)
Longer pedicle (8–13 cm) than TUG or SGAP; well-concealed gluteal crease scar

donor_site.closure: Layered primary closure 1 cm below inferior gluteal crease.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine frog-leg (two-team breast surgery) or prone.
preoperative_planning: MRA or CTA to localize dominant profunda perforator
technique.design: Transverse crescentic ellipse 1 cm below gluteal crease; vertical height ≤6–7 cm.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise anterior border over gracilis and expose adductor magnus fascia.
2. Dissect posteriorly to identify dominant profunda perforator.
3. Split adductor magnus fibers along perforator to profunda femoris vessels.
4. Bevel inferior subcutaneous fat carefully without flattening buttock.
5. Transfer to internal mammary vessels and close crease in layers.
pearls: Keep superior incision 1 cm below gluteal fold to prevent scar migration.
pitfalls: Designing vertical height >7–8 cm causing painful dehiscence.

references.book: Blondeel PN et al. Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Superior Gluteal Artery Perforator (SGAP) Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Posterior division of internal iliac artery

perforators.label: SGA Emergence Zone
perforators.location: Junction of medial and middle thirds of line from PSIS to greater trochanter
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Courses obliquely through gluteus maximus superior to piriformis

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Thin-walled gluteal veins near piriformis require meticulous clipping.
vascular_variants: Gluteus maximus thickness influences harvest depth and pedicle length

dimensions.thickness_notes: Firm, dense gluteal adipose tissue provides strong projection.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Pedicled V-Y/propeller covers sacral pressure injuries; free flap reconstructs breast.

indications: Stage IV sacral pressure injury reconstruction (pedicled muscle-sparing)
Alternative autologous breast reconstruction when abdomen and thighs are unavailable
contraindications: Prior gluteal liposuction or radiation violating SGA perforators
advantages: Preserves gluteus maximus muscle (essential in ambulatory sacral wound patients)
Available even in slender patients lacking abdominal tissue
disadvantages: Deep intramuscular dissection through thick gluteus maximus

preoperative_planning: Handheld Doppler along PSIS–greater trochanter line
technique.design: Oblique ellipse over lateral-most strong SGA perforator for maximum pedicle length.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate suprafascially from lateral to medial over gluteus maximus.
2. Select a large lateral perforator for maximal pedicle length.
3. Split gluteus maximus fibers longitudinally down to sacral fascia.
4. Control deep venous tributaries carefully.
5. Advance pedicled island into sacral defect, or divide for free transfer.
pearls: Leaves inferior gluteal territory intact for future sacral recurrence.
pitfalls: Deep venous avulsion within thick gluteus maximus.

references.book: Blondeel PN et al. Perforator Flaps: Anatomy, Technique, & Clinical Applications

name: Gastrocnemius Muscle Flap (Medial & Lateral Heads)

classification.mathes_nahai: Type I (single dominant sural pedicle per head)

tissue_components: Medial or lateral gastrocnemius muscle head

dominant_pedicle.artery: Medial sural artery (medial head) or Lateral sural artery (lateral head)
dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Popliteal artery at knee joint level
dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired medial or lateral sural venae comitantes

perforators.label: Medial Sural Hilum
perforators.location: 2–4 cm below popliteal crease on deep surface of medial head
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Proximal entry allows wide anterior sweep across knee and proximal tibia

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Medial head is larger and reaches farther anteriorly than lateral head.
vascular_variants: Rare common sural trunk from popliteal artery

sensory: Common peroneal nerve (fibular neck — protect with lateral head)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Protect sural nerve in midline raphe.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Grid-scoring the deep epimysium adds 2–3 cm reach and extra width.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Workhorse for anterior knee, exposed total knee arthroplasty (TKA) prosthesis, patellar tendon, and proximal third of tibia.

indications: Exposed total knee arthroplasty (TKA) prosthesis or infected knee joint
Proximal-third tibial Gustilo IIIB open fractures with exposed bone/hardware
contraindications: Popliteal occlusion or sural pedicle trauma
Middle- or distal-third tibial defects (beyond reach)
advantages: Fast, reliable pedicled regional harvest without microsurgery
Rich vascular muscle bed ideal for infected prosthetic wounds

donor_site.closure: Primary posterior-medial calf closure; STSG over transposed muscle.
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal for ambulation when soleus and opposite head remain intact.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with hip externally rotated and knee flexed.
preoperative_planning: Prefer medial head unless defect strictly superolateral
technique.design: Longitudinal incision 2 cm posterior to medial tibial border.
harvest_steps: 1. Develop plane between gastrocnemius and soleus (plantaris tendon marks plane).
2. Separate medial and lateral heads along midline raphe protecting sural nerve.
3. Divide medial head distally at Achilles aponeurosis leaving 1-cm fascial cuff.
4. Grid-score deep investing fascia to expand reach by 2–3 cm.
5. Transpose anteriorly to knee/proximal tibia (divide tight skin bridge rather than strangulating) and cover with STSG.
pearls: Plantaris tendon is the definitive landmark between gastrocnemius and soleus.
pitfalls: Compressing common peroneal nerve at fibular neck during lateral head transposition.

recipient_vessels_options: Pedicled on medial or lateral sural artery

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Pectoralis Major Muscle / Myocutaneous Flap

classification.mathes_nahai: Type V (dominant thoracoacromial + secondary segmental internal mammary perforators)

minor_pedicles: Internal mammary perforators (2nd–5th interspaces — sternal turnover)

perforators.label: Inferomedial Skin Island
perforators.location: Inferomedial to nipple-areolar complex over 5th–7th ribs
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Pedicle follows acromion–xiphoid line curving down from mid-clavicle

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Turnover flap requires intact ipsilateral IMA (verify CABG LIMA harvest!).
vascular_variants: Prior LIMA CABG harvest precludes left sternal turnover (use thoracoacromial advancement instead)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Bulky myocutaneous paddle in obese/female patients; muscle-only ideal for sternal wounds.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Workhorse for deep sternal wounds (advancement or turnover) and head & neck salvage (carotid coverage, pharynx, floor of mouth).

indications: Deep sternal wound infection / mediastinitis (bilateral advancement or turnover)
Head & neck salvage (carotid protection, pharyngocutaneous fistula, failed free flap)
contraindications: Prior LIMA/RIMA harvest contraindicates ipsilateral turnover flap
advantages: Dependable regional workhorse requiring no microsurgery
Dual Mathes–Nahai Type V versatility (advancement vs turnover)

donor_site.closure: Primary chest wall closure over drains.
donor_site.functional_loss: Mild decrease in horizontal shoulder adduction.

technique.design: For sternum: mobilize through sternotomy wound; for H&N: paddle inferomedial to nipple.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate subcutaneous plane off pectoralis major laterally to deltopectoral groove.
2. Detach sternal/costal origins medially while visualizing thoracoacromial pedicle on deep surface.
3. Release humeral insertion if additional medial advancement is needed.
4. For H&N PMMC, tack skin dermis to fascia and pass through wide neck tunnel.
pearls: Tack skin paddle dermis to muscle fascia to prevent perforator shear.
pitfalls: Raising a left sternal turnover flap after LIMA harvest.

recipient_vessels_options: Pedicled on thoracoacromial artery or internal mammary perforators

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications

name: Paramedian Forehead Flap

dominant_pedicle.veins: Supratrochlear veins draining to angular/facial vein

minor_pedicles: Angular and supraorbital anastomotic arcade at medial canthus

perforators.label: Supratrochlear Orbital Rim Exit
perforators.location: 1.7–2.2 cm lateral to midline at medial superior orbital rim
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Pierces corrugator supercilii and becomes subcutaneous ~1.5–2 cm above brow

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: 1.2–1.5 cm pedicle base reliably captures artery and venous plexus without kinking.
vascular_variants: Emergence varies 1.5–2.5 cm from midline — confirm with Doppler

motor: Frontal branch of facial nerve lies lateral — protect
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Forehead scalp numbness superior to donor site.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Unmatched color, texture, and sebaceous match for nasal subunits; use 3-stage thinning in smokers.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Medial brow / corrugator base (1.7–2.2 cm from midline)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches entire nose (tip, columella, ala, dorsum, sidewall) and medial canthus.

indications: Gold standard for major nasal defects (>1.5–2 cm), multi-subunit defects, or exposed cartilage/bone
Nasal tip, alar, and columellar reconstruction
contraindications: Prior trauma dividing both supratrochlear pedicles
Inability to tolerate staged pedicle division at 3 weeks
advantages: Best facial skin color and texture match for the nose
Robust axial vascularity with narrow 1.2–1.5 cm base

donor_site.closure: Lower forehead closed primarily; superior gap (>3.5 cm) heals remarkably well by secondary intention.

preoperative_planning: Doppler supratrochlear artery at medial brow
technique.design: Trace subunit template along vertical axis of supratrochlear artery with 1.2–1.5 cm pedicle base.
harvest_steps: 1. Complete nasal subunit excision (Burget–Menick) and build cartilage support + lining.
2. Verify reach from medial brow to nasal tip with gauze template.
3. Elevate distally subcutaneously (or subgaleal in smokers), transitioning subperiosteally 1.5 cm above rim.
4. Transpose 180° onto nose without tension.
5. Stage 2 (3 weeks): divide pedicle, re-inset medial brow without medializing brows.
pearls: Allow upper forehead gap to heal by secondary intention rather than distorting brows.
pitfalls: Aggressive primary distal thinning in active smokers causing tip necrosis.

recipient_vessels_options: Interpolated axial pedicle on supratrochlear artery

name: Groin Flap (SCIA / SCIP)

classification.perforator_type: Direct cutaneous / Superficial or deep branch of SCIA

dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Femoral artery ~2–3 cm inferior to inguinal ligament
dominant_pedicle.veins: Superficial circumflex iliac vein (SCIV) + small venae comitantes

perforators.label: Superficial & Deep SCIA Branches
perforators.location: 2 cm below and parallel to inguinal ligament crossing sartorius toward ASIS
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Include sartorius fascia medial to its lateral border to protect deep branch

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: SCIV drains reliably into saphenous bulb.
vascular_variants: Small caliber (<1 mm) makes free SCIP supermicrosurgery demanding

sensory: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (near ASIS — protect)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Protect LFCN to avoid lateral thigh paresthesia.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thin in lean patients (especially SCIP elevated above Scarpa fascia).

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Medial border of sartorius (~2 cm below inguinal ligament)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Pedicled distant attachment for dorsal/volar hand and multi-digit degloving (divide at 3 weeks); free SCIP for thin resurfacing.

indications: Salvage pedicled coverage for complex hand, wrist, or multi-digit degloving injuries
Ultra-thin free SCIP flap for foot, hand, or head & neck resurfacing

donor_site.closure: Primary closure with hip slightly flexed.

preoperative_planning: Handheld Doppler 2 cm inferior to inguinal ligament from femoral pulse toward ASIS
technique.design: Axis 2 cm inferior and parallel to inguinal ligament extending lateral to ASIS.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate lateral-to-medial above deep fascia.
2. At lateral border of sartorius, incise sartorius fascia and include it medially.
3. Stop ~2 cm lateral to femoral artery for pedicled flap.
4. Tube pedicle bridge, inset onto hand, and divide at 3 weeks.
pearls: Include sartorius fascia medial to the lateral border of sartorius.
pitfalls: Injuring LFCN near ASIS or allowing arm weight to avulse inset.

references.book: Zenn MR, Jones G. Reconstructive Surgery: Anatomy, Technique, and Clinical Applications
